channel.title: Security Brief
channel.description: Original analysis and ranked cybersecurity news with links to original sources

item.title: The edge is where attackers get in: this week's firewall, VPN and remote-access exploits
item.description: Five exploited flaws in firewalls, VPNs, remote-support software and file-sharing servers show one pattern. The systems that sit at the edge of your network, and that administrators manage remotely, are the weakest link. Here is what to check first.

item.title: October 2026 Patch Tuesday: what the Microsoft feed shows and what to do
item.description: The Microsoft feed lists few entries, and most of them are updates to October's release rather than new fixes. The one item that needs planning is a .NET remote code execution flaw that Microsoft has not fixed yet. Identity Web and WSL need version checks if you use them.

item.title: Weekly M365 & Entra Briefing: 13 to 19 October 2026
item.description: Exchange sign-in problems after October Windows Server updates, an identity-based incident at ConnectWise that affected Microsoft 365 tenants, and why device-code abuse is still worth a Conditional Access check.

item.title: Max-Severity GitLab Vulnerability Exploited Against Alpine Linux
item.description: Tracked as CVE-2026-97229, the bug allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server. The post Max-Severity GitLab Vulnerability Exploited Against Alpine Linux appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: New Cisco firewall zero-day exploited to crash SSL VPN devices
item.description: Cisco released security updates to patch a denial-of-service zero-day in Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) and Threat Defense (FTD) software that attackers are exploiting to remotely crash vulnerable firewall devices.

item.title: CISA Confirms Active Exploitation of Two PHP2Shell Flaws Enabling Remote Code Execution
item.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Monday confirmed active exploitation of the recently patched PHP2Shell flaws by adding them to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The PHP vulnerabilities, both rated 9.2 on the CVSS scoring system, facilitate unauthenticated remote…

item.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Friday added two vulnerabilities impacting Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV), citing reports of active exploitation in the wild. item.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Tuesday added two vulnerabilities impacting Adobe Commerce and Magento, and Google's Brotli decoder library to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation. item.title: Hackers exploit Cisco SD-WAN flaw to deploy custom KeyDrift malware
item.description: A newly identified advanced persistent threat (APT) group tracked as UAT-11473 was observed exploiting CVE-2026-20127, an authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controllers, to deploy a custom malware framework called KeyDrift.

item.title: Drupal Commerce Core Vulnerability Exploited Against Online Stores
item.description: Drupal says a highly critical Commerce Core access bypass is exploited in the wild and urges store owners to audit their orders. The post Drupal Commerce Core Vulnerability Exploited Against Online Stores appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Drupal warns of critical Commerce Core flaw exploited in attacks
item.description: Drupal warned admins to patch a critical access bypass vulnerability in the Commerce Core module that attackers are exploiting in the wild.

item.title: Chinese Hackers Quietly Used Low-Severity ESXi Logging Flaw as Zero-Day
item.description: CVE-2026-41709 allows attackers with administrative privileges to perform operations without being logged. The post Chinese Hackers Quietly Used Low-Severity ESXi Logging Flaw as Zero-Day appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: ShinyHunters-Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day Turns Out to Be Three Chained Flaws
item.description: The critical Oracle PeopleSoft bug that ShinyHunters has exploited since May is not one flaw but three chained together, the researchers who reported it said this week. Oracle patched all three under a single identifier, CVE-2026-35273, in June. Its root is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) that reaches an internal…

item.title: Apple Backports Fix for Exploited CoreGraphics Flaw to Older iPhones and iPads
item.description: Apple on Monday backported fixes for a high-severity security flaw that was exploited in real-world cyber attacks to older devices. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-86950 (CVSS score: 8.8), is an out-of-bounds write affecting CoreGraphics that could result in arbitrary code execution when processing a…

item.title: CISA says max severity GitLab flaw now exploited in the wild
item.description: Attackers have started exploiting a maximum-severity GitLab vulnerability patched earlier this month, according to the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA).

item.title: Binance Suffers Security Breach Affecting $6.3 Billion in Assets, Nearly $3 Billion Frozen
item.description: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that a "security incident" on its platform has impacted about $6.3 billion worth of assets. The world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange said nearly $3 billion of those assets have been frozen on-chain so far. Tether and Circle said they have frozen more than 1.567 billion…

item.title: Binance probes potential $5.8 billion crypto-theft hack
item.description: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance is investigating a potential security breach involving up to $5.8 billion in digital assets, in what could become the largest cryptocurrency hack in history.

item.title: Claude Model Builds Exploits Across Major Browsers & OSes
item.description: An unreleased version of the AI model has found and chained multiple vulnerabilities in Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, and Linux, Anthropic says.

item.description: As Microsoft Threat Intelligence continues to track how threat actors operationalize AI to increase the speed, efficiency, and complexity of attacks, we’ve identified North Korean threat actors expanding their use of AI with varying levels of adoption. item.description: In der Microsoft Authenticator-App für Android gab es eine Schwachstelle CVE-2026-80097, über die Angreifer auf Inhalte und Geheimnisse zugreifen konnten. item.title: CVE-2026-88078 Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) Spoofing Vulnerability
item.description: CWE added. Informational change only.

item.title: CVE-2026-62877 Windows Win32k Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
item.description: Added supported editions of Microsoft Office to the Security Updates table because they are affected by this vulnerability. Microsoft recommends that customers running any of these editions of Office install the latest security updates to be fully protected from this vulnerability.

item.title: Even after PHP2Shell, blast radius matters more than a CVSS score
item.description: PHP2Shell shows how quickly attackers can exploit critical vulnerabilities, often before organizations have time to patch. Token Security explains why limiting the access of service accounts, API keys, and AI agents is just as important as fixing vulnerabilities to reduce the damage from a breach.

item.title: Japan's GMO urges customers to shut down PCs amid ransomware threat
item.description: The GMO Group has urged customers to disconnect their systems from the internet and shut down computers after a threat actor who breached the company's Onamae Desktop Cloud threatened to launch a ransomware attack today.

item.title: Exposed Infrastructure Reveals How Ransomware Affiliates Used AI Agents to Execute Intrusions
item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have discovered an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven intrusion ecosystem run by affiliates of the INC and The Gentlemen ransomware groups. Central to the operation is an "Autonomous Red Team Kill Chain Framework" referred to as Phantom. The threat actor is assessed to be Russian-speaking…

item.title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in record crypto heist
item.description: Binance has suspended all withdrawals after the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange fell victim to what appears to be the biggest heist in history. The exchange put the “estimated total impact” of the hack at about $6.3 billion and said around $3 billion of affected assets, mainly stablecoins that act as cash for…

item.title: Bulletproof Host Virtualine Loses Its Domain to FBI Seizure
item.description: It allowed customers to host hack-for-hire services, supported ransomware and infostealer operators, and accepted crypto payments. The post Bulletproof Host Virtualine Loses Its Domain to FBI Seizure appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Hackers target government Windows systems in Asia with new malware
item.description: The previously unknown malware, dubbed NetamLoader, uses legitimate Microsoft software components to execute malicious code, evade security tools and download additional programs onto infected computers.

item.title: Microsoft finally fixes VPN issues caused by September updates
item.description: Microsoft has resolved Always On VPN connection failures triggered after installing the September 2026 Windows 11 security updates.

item.title: Binance links $6.3 billion crypto theft to compromised DevOps laptop
item.description: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, has linked the theft of about $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency to a DevOps engineer's compromised laptop.

item.description: Drupal has warned that threat actors are exploiting a "highly critical" security flaw in its Commerce Core component. item.title: Binance hit by record $6.3 billion crypto hack, scrambles to freeze funds
item.description: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, confirmed that it had been hacked in a $6.3 billion heist that blockchain investigators are blaming on North Korea.

item.title: Japan Airlines suffers third-party data breach exposing passenger info
item.description: Japan Airlines (JAL) has announced that a data breach at Amadeus's Passenger Service System exposed the data of about 92,000 customers.

item.title: Polymarket halts trading after crypto-draining script breach, $2.5M traced
item.description: Prediction market platform Polymarket temporarily suspended trading on Thursday after hackers compromised a third-party service to distribute cryptocurrency-draining JavaScript, with approximately $2.5 million in assets traced to a suspected attacker wallet.

item.title: Limited reports of PHP bug exploitation emerge
item.description: One cyber firm listed a half-dozen exploitations of the PHP2Shell bugs, and another identified a well targeted, suspected Chinese campaign that breached U.S. "government affiliated" servers.

item.description: Some attacks take real skill. Others just need someone to leave a door open. This week has both. item.title: BYOD cyberattack diverts ambulances and cancels classes at University of New Mexico health center
item.description: Ambulances were diverted, surgeries cancelled, and medical students sent home from classes after a ransomware group attacked the University of New Mexico's Health Sciences Center (HSC) this week. Read more in my article on the Fortra blog.

item.title: Microsoft fixes Remote Desktop failures caused by recent Windows updates
item.description: Microsoft has resolved a known issue that prevents non-admin users from connecting to devices via Remote Desktop when the "Administrator protection" security feature is enabled.

item.title: Windows 11 KB5127936 update released with 41 changes and fixes
item.description: Microsoft released the KB5127936 preview cumulative update for Windows 11 versions 25H2 and 26H2, with 41 changes, including File Explorer and Cloud rebuild improvements.

item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of what appears to be an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted attack orchestrated by a suspected China-nexus threat actor that has leveraged the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to breach exposed systems. item.title: Ukrainian Hive and Nefilim Ransomware Affiliate Gets 70 Months in US Prison
item.description: Artem Stryzhak was sentenced to 70 months in prison after pleading guilty to using Nefilim ransomware in attacks. The post Ukrainian Hive and Nefilim Ransomware Affiliate Gets 70 Months in US Prison appeared first on SecurityWeek.
